p: and send portions to whoever has nothing prepared,
כִּי קָדוֹשׁ הַיּוֹם לַאֲדוֹנֵינוּ (נְחֶמְיָה ח, י),
for the day is holy to our Lord" (Nechemiah 8:10);
עַל יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
about the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah.
because the day is holy to Hashem,
for that reason they should eat rich foods?
Is there not in the Gemara (Pesachim 68b)
the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua,
whether half of it is for Hashem or all of it is for Hashem,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים טז, ח) לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ,
because it says (Devarim 16:8) "for Hashem your G-d,"
implies that it is not for you.
we find that Rabbi Eliezer said to his students,
עִנְיַן יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah,
the time of man's creation — why is it for joy?
"It would have been better for him not to have been created
that there are those who fast on Rosh Hashanah,
and there is no mitzvah specifically to eat and drink;
so the above pasuk requires explanation.
However, the matter is, as is known,
that on every Rosh Hashanah there is aroused
as we say (in the Mussaf prayer),
and of that time it is said (Koheles 7:29),
and after that came the corruption
עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע.
through eating from the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil.
And it is brought in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar 69a)
that the Rabbanan hold it was wheat,
some say it was a vine,
and others say it was a fig, etc.,
"and all of it is true," etc.
And in every dispute it is known
that "these and these are the words of the living G-d,"
since the Tikkunim state it explicitly.
For the Tree of Knowledge and the Tree of Life
were in the middle of the garden,
with all the trees of the garden around them,
הַטַּעַם שֶׁל כָּל עֲצֵי הַגָּן כּוּלָּם,
the taste of all the trees of the garden;
וְאִם הָיָה טוֹעֵם בַּתְּחִלָּה מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים,
had he tasted first from the Tree of Life,
בְּכָל הַפֵּירוֹת טַעַם שֶׁל עֵץ הַחַיִּים.
the taste of the Tree of Life in all the fruits.
But when he tasted from the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,
that one feels in all foods
the taste of the Tree of Knowledge,
which is the desire for eating
And on the day of Rosh Hashanah,
on which some opinions permit fasting,
this is because on that day
to repair the first blemish, of the desire for eating;
which is the aspect of iskafya, subduing,
so that the yetzer hara is subdued
and through this he can repair
And the mitzvah of shofar on Rosh Hashanah as well
is for the arousal of the shofar
as is brought in Pesikta Rabbasi (beginning of piska 39)
they are destined to be redeemed from the Angel of Death;
that then the yetzer hara will be eradicated from the world,
and this through the great shofar,
"And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar will be sounded,
and those lost in the land of Ashur will come,
and those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim";
meaning that the first blemish will be repaired
among the nations of the world
will have aroused within them the inner
as at the beginning of Creation.
And as is brought in the Yerushalmi
(הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז, ב, ד״ה כְּדֵי)
(cited in Tosafos Rosh Hashanah 16b, s.v. Kedei):
"When he hears the sound of the shofar
the first time, he is alarmed" —
the Satan, who is the yetzer hara —
"he says, 'The time has come to be swallowed up.'"
For in truth on every Rosh Hashanah
of the sounding of the great shofar Above,
Therefore there comes also the mitzvah on our part
so that we too, from our side, are aroused by this
the plain blast before it and the plain blast after it:
that is, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
Who at first made man upright —
this is the tekiah before it;
and the plain blast after it
is as it will be in the time to come,
when everything will return to the first rectification
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and the teruah in the middle
is the present rectification from the side of man.
why they instituted in the text of the prayer,
in the ten pesukim of Shofaros,
to say the pesukim from Kesuvim
about Malchuyos and Zichronos as well:
אַךְ הוּא מִפְּנֵי סְמִיכַת פְּסוּקֵי שׁוֹפָרוֹת
But it is because of the sequence of the pesukim of Shofaros,
which are "made in truth and uprightness" (Tehillim 111:8);
for in the three pesukim of the Torah
are mentioned the sounds of the shofar
which alludes to the plain blast before it,
for then there was a rectification of the corruption
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, ד)
"When they heard 'You shall have no other gods,'
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart";
and about this it is said (Tehillim 82:6),
And in the three pesukim of the Kesuvim
נִזְכָּר עִנְיַן מִצְוַת תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר מִצִּידֵּנוּ,
is mentioned the mitzvah of blowing the shofar on our part,
which alludes to the teruah in the middle,
And in the three pesukim of Nevi'im
are mentioned the sounds of the shofar of the time to come,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
when the rectification will be completed from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
alluding to the plain blast after it, as above.
And as a result of this
תִּקְּנוּ גַּם סֵדֶר פְּסוּקֵי מַלְכֻיּוֹת וְזִכְרוֹנוֹת
they arranged the pesukim of Malchuyos and Zichronos too
Let us return to our subject:
שֶׁעִנְיַן הַתַּעֲנִית שֶׁל יוֹם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
the fast of the day of Rosh Hashanah
is a rectification of the aspect of iskafya, subduing.
וְיֵשׁ עוֹד תִּיקּוּן בְּמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה,
And there is another rectification on a higher level,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה עַצְמָהּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
that is, that through the eating itself, in holiness,
so that it will be like eating from the Tree of Life,
which is a Tree of Life.
And to this the prophet alluded for them:
and wherever eating and drinking appear,
the verse is speaking of words of Torah,
and drink of the wine I have mixed."
And rich foods and sweet drinks in particular
allude to sensing the taste and the delight
as is brought in the Gemara (Bava Basra 22a):
"They ate fat meat at Rava's house,"
that is, halachos with good reasoning.
And this is "for the day is holy, etc.":
one can do everything in holiness.
"and send portions to whoever has nothing prepared,"
yet we do not find such a mitzvah
But it alludes to what Chazal said
with Torah and acts of kindness,
his yetzer is given over into his hand,"
אַשְׁרֵיכֶם זוֹרְעֵי עַל כָּל מָיִם וְגוֹ׳;
"Fortunate are you who sow beside all waters, etc.";
"who sow" means charity and acts of kindness,
and this is the repair of the blemish for the future.
"Whoever occupies himself with Torah and acts of kindness
'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned';
and this is the repair of the blemish of the past.
And to this it alludes here:
and these are the culmination of the rectification.
that they occupied themselves with Torah until midday,
he said to them, "Eat rich foods."
וְהִנֵּה מִקּוֹדֶם זֶה נֶאֱמַר (נְחֶמְיָה ח, ט)
and Ezra the Kohen said to the people,
וְגַם אַחַר זֶה נֶאֱמַר (שָׁם ט, ה)
and also after this it says (ibid. 9:5),
does it say simply, "And he said,
that it is the statement of Nechemiah alone.
that the enemies of Yehudah sent him:
to proclaim, 'There is a king in Yehudah,'"
and he answered them that the thing was false.
If so, why was it written down —
Did not our Sages of blessed memory say
that the Torah recorded invented words
only for the sake of peace?
there was then in him a spark of kingship
for he was governor in Yehudah;
and as our Sages of blessed memory said (Shevuos 16a),
that he sanctified the wall with two thanksgiving offerings;
does it not require a king
that they had the aspect of a king,
that they appointed him as king —
not to rebel against the king of Persia,
only so that he would have the status of a king
And it is brought in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 6):
"The heart in the body is like a king in the land";
and therefore Nechemiah had this power
in the heart of all of Yisrael together,
so that the rectification would come
"for the joy of Hashem is your strength";
and especially according to the statement of Chazal
and in him there shone something of the rectification
as is known from the holy sefarim,
and in keeping with what we said above.
And he said, "And do not be saddened,
for the joy of Hashem, etc." —
from fasting one can come to sadness,
while their main strength is joy in Hashem,
as we say (in the prayers of the Yamim Nora'im),
"And so the righteous will see and rejoice, etc.";
the mouth of the accusers is stopped:
"and iniquity will close its mouth, etc."
that this is why it concludes there (Nechemiah 8:12),
for they understood the words, etc."
that they felt in the heart the holiness of the day,
and their heart was filled with holiness
and also with joy in Hashem,
and that is the sensing of Hashem Yisbarach.
as meaning that Hashem Yisbarach is in joy —
and therefore he said, "Do not be saddened,"
as they said in the Zohar, Tetzaveh
in the passage beginning "Come and see," etc.:
And this is the meaning of "for they understood, etc.":
that through their deeds they arouse Above —
וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה
they would arouse great joy Above.
Until here, from his holy manuscript.
